title: fast-path-fallback-execution-runbook
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Summary:
This runbook defines the fast-path fallback execution flow for model-serving incidents where primary inference pools or low-latency model variants become unavailable or breach critical SLOs. It is intended for on-call SREs, incident commanders, and platform engineers responsible for multi-tenant inference availability and graceful degradation.

Scope:
- Applies to Redwood-hosted inference gateways and Dedicated clusters.
- Covers automated and manual fallback to: cheaper/quantized model variants, cross-region pools, and cached responses.
- Excludes long-term capacity reprovisioning; see capacity-onboarding-runway for that flow.

Goals and SLO thresholds that trigger this runbook:
- Primary trigger: generation.latency.p99 > 1.5x SLO for a sustained 5m window OR generation.errors.rate > 0.5% for 3m.
- Secondary trigger: error budget burn rate > 4x over a 1h window for any tenant-level SLO.
- Safety guard: do not execute cross-tenant eviction unless verified by the Incident Commander and Product Lead.

Pre-flight checks (first 5 minutes):
1) Identify scope and blast radius
   - Determine affected services: gateway (edge-proxy), router (redwood-router), serving pool(s) (model-pool-<id>), and downstream queues.
   - Command: `rctl incident inspect --alert $ALERT_ID --format brief`
2) Verify telemetry and alerts
   - Check Grafana dashboard: `SLO / generation / latency & errors`
   - Run quick queries in `slo-monitor`: `slo-monitor query --metric generation.latency.p99 --window 5m --filter service=<service>`
3) Pager and stakeholders
   - Confirm the on-call owner for serving-runtime and platform. Notify product for tenants >$contract_threshold.

Fast-path fallback decision matrix (summary):
- If p99 latency spike only and error rate low -> enable request-batching guardrail and increase tail batch size (automated attempt 1).
- If error rate high OR p99 + error spike -> trigger model-variant fallback and traffic routing to backup pool.
- If both latency and error budget burning rapidly -> enable cached prefixes and emergency rate limit.

Automated actions (order of execution; prefer automation where available):
1) Attempt soft-guard adjustments (automated):
   - Enable continuous batching tuner for the affected pool: `cap-orch apply --pool <id> --tuner continuous-batching --profile tail-optimized`
   - Expected outcome: reduced per-token latency variance within 90s.
2) Model-variant fallback (automated with circuit-breaker):
   - Policy: route up to 30% of traffic to quantized-variant-v1 for 5m, then ramp if stable.
   - Command (manual override): `router route-set --service <svc> --policy fallback:quantized-variant-v1 --initial-weight 30 --ramp 5m`
   - Verify with `traffic-observer tail --service <svc> --metric upstream_errors,latency --window 2m`
3) Cross-region pool warmup (manual if automation fails):
   - Steps: reserve ephemeral capacity in region B, pre-warm model weights, and add to routing table.
   - Commands: `cap-orch reserve --region us-west-2 --gpus 4 --ttl 2h` then `prewarm-warmup --pool <new> --model <model-id> --kv-cache true`
4) Activate emergency cached-responses and degraded-mode (manual, with notice to product):
   - Degraded mode returns cached completions for known prompt classes and a short explanatory header.
   - Toggle: `edge-proxy toggle --service <svc> --feature degraded-cache --enable`
5) Apply tenant-level throttles (last resort prior to eviction):
   - Use token-priority controller to reduce best-effort consumption: `throttlectl set --tenant <tenant-id> --limit rps=... --priority best-effort`

Manual action checklist (for Incident Commander):
1) Confirm trigger and scope.
2) Execute model-variant fallback if automation unsuccessful.
3) Approve cross-region capacity if fallback does not restore SLOs within 10 minutes.
4) Authorize tenant throttles or evictions only after product and legal are informed (for enterprise customers, require exec approval).

Observability and verification (what to watch):
- Dashboards: SLO / generation / p50, p90, p99; errors.rate; token-cost-per-request.
- Key logs: model-pool logs (server-stats), redwood-router decisions, prewarm traces.
- Alerts to clear: generation.latency.p99, generation.errors.rate, model-pool.cpu-temp.
- Verify success criteria: p99 back within 1.1x SLO and error-rate < 0.1% sustained for 10m after mitigation.

Runbook play-by-play (detailed procedure):
- Minutes 0–5: Run pre-flight checks; gather quick evidence (traces, flamegraphs). Set priority: fast-path fallback.
- Minutes 5–15: Trigger automated soft-guard adjustments (step 1). If no improvement, initiate model-variant fallback (step 2).
- Minutes 15–40: Monitor fallback impact; if not stable, begin cross-region warmup and incremental routing changes (step 3).
- Minutes 40–90: Consider degraded cache and tenant throttles. Prepare communications: status-page update, customer PQs for affected tenants.
- Post-stabilization: start a targeted post-incident evaluation (see 'Post-incident tasks').

Playbook for common scenarios (examples):
1) Quantization regression after recent rollout
   - If errors spike immediately after a quantized-variant rollout: rollback variant, inspect quantization-profile, and run `eval-harness --promptset regression-suite --model <variant>`
2) Sudden cross-region network partition
   - If region A -> region B networking fails: route traffic to alternate region only if cross-region latency < 80ms and warmup success is confirmed. If cross-region latency high, enable degraded-cache.
3) Embedded-heavy workloads (high token retention use)
   - Prioritize KV-cache enabled pools and increase max-batch-bytes for that tenant pool. Notify cost/finance for potential burst charge implications.

Safety and guardrails:
- Circuit-breaker timeouts: automated fallback will abort if error-rate on fallback rises >1% within 3m.
- Max cross-region spill: default 40% of traffic unless approved by Incident Commander.
- Eviction policy: follow multi-tenant eviction-runbook; only evict best-effort non-enterprise tenants after approval.

Owner and contact matrix:
- Primary on-call: serving-runtime (pager: @serving-runtime-oncall)
- Secondary: eng-sre-runbooks (pager: @sre-runbooks)
- Platform escalation: platform-oncall (pager: @platform-oncall)
- Product / Customer success notification: notify if customer SLA affected (email: enterprise-ops@redwood.ai)

Operational tooling and commands (reference):
- rctl (incident tooling): inspect, annotate, escalate.
- cap-orch (capacity orchestrator): reserve, prewarm, apply tuners.
- router (redwood-router): route-set, route-status.
- slo-monitor: query, compare, alert-suppress.
- edge-proxy: toggle degraded cache, set-rate-limits.
- Example commands: `rctl annotate --incident $ID --note "Fallback to quantized-variant-v1 applied"`

Communications template (status page and Slack):
- Status page short: "Degraded performance impacting text-generation in region us-east-1. Traffic is being routed to fallback model variants to restore availability; customers may see reduced throughput and shorter completions. We will provide updates every 15 minutes."
- Slack update format: `#incident-<$ID> | status: fallback applied | owner: <IC> | impact: <#tenants> | mitigation: quantized-variant-v1(30%->100%)`

Post-incident tasks (within 72h):
1) Evidence collection: attach traces, sample requests, and traffic graphs to incident ticket.
2) Root cause hypothesis: lead by serving-runtime and validated by applied-ml team.
3) Capacity adjustments: if cross-region warmups used, evaluate reserve-to-commit conversion.
4) Runbook updates: add any missing steps or failed automations to this document.
5) SLO adjustment proposal if necessary: submit to SLO governance board with data.

Metrics to capture for retrospective:
- Time to partial mitigation (first automated action)
- Time to stable (SLO within 1.1x)
- Number of tenants affected and any enterprise impacts
- Fallback success rate and fallback error delta

Appendix A — Quick reference table (commands & expected outcomes):
- `cap-orch apply --pool p-23 --tuner continuous-batching`: expected reduce tail p99 in 60–120s
- `router route-set --service s-generation --policy fallback:quantized-variant-v1 --initial-weight 30`: expected error delta < 0.2%, latency change +/− 15%
- `edge-proxy toggle --service s-generation --feature degraded-cache --enable`: expected to restore availability while reducing freshness for cached prompt classes

Appendix B — Troubleshooting checklist (if fallback makes things worse):
1) Revert fallback weights to prior state.
2) Scale down batch size if batching introduced instability.
3) Isolate tenant causing disproportionate errors and throttle.
4) Escalate to model-onboarding team for fast rollback if variant appears corrupted.
